title: Disruptions in Strait of Hormuz Threaten International Shipments
text:
• Disruptions in and around the Strait of Hormuz threaten to slow international shipments.
• The US imposed a blockade on traffic entering or leaving Iranian ports after US-Iran talks failed.
• The US military's blockade of ships in the Strait of Hormuz took effect on Monday.
• The Strait of Hormuz links the Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
• No vessels have passed the US naval forces during the first 48 hours of the blockade, according to US Central Command.
• The commander of Iran's joint military command threatened to halt trade in the Gulf region if the US does not lift its blockade on Iranian ports.
• At least 15 US warships formed the blockade of Iranian ports, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations.
• 20,000 seafarers and approximately 1,600 vessels were stuck in the Gulf on Monday evening, according to International Maritime Organization Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez.
• The price for a barrel of Brent crude increased by 0.1 percent to settle at $94.93 on Wednesday.
• The Strait of Hormuz carries approximately 20 million barrels of oil daily, which is 20 percent of the world's daily oil supply and one-third of seaborne oil supply.
• Iran exported 1.84 million barrels per day of crude oil in March and 1.71 million barrels per day in April.
• Trump has repeatedly pressed for free passage for global shipping through the Strait.
• Iran has been allowing a small number of ships to go through the shipping channel since the war began on Feb. 28.
• Iran wants ships to coordinate with its forces and pay a toll.
• Two Iran-linked vessels got through on Monday before the US blockade.
• Before the US-Israel war on Iran began, there were 130 daily crossings.
• German shipping giant Hapag-Lloyd said its vessels would not be sailing through the Strait over safety concerns.
• Ships will be forced to find longer shipping paths, raising the cost of fuel.
• Iran dubbed the US blockade "piracy".
• Trump warned that any Iranian "fast-attack" ships that go near the US blockade would be "eliminated".
• Several US allies in Europe refused to join the US blockade.
• French President Emmanuel Macron and Britain will co-host a virtual meeting this week to forge an international coalition that guarantees passage for ships in the Strait.
• The UN spokesperson urged all sides to ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait.
• The Strait is a key global transportation route for fertilizer.
• The UN Food and Agriculture Organization warned that the crisis could lead to higher food prices globally.
